note: Focusing heavily on long-term maintainability, operational stability, and debuggability from a PM/future-maintainer perspective.

findings.section: Wave 1 — System-Wide Process Discovery and Daemon Core
findings.message: The plan specifies WMI for process discovery but fails to define a signature registry or heuristic classification engine. A future maintainer needs a clear, updateable mechanism (e.g., regex patterns, command-line arguments, parent-child process chains) to distinguish an 'AI-related process' from a normal user process. Without this, the system will drown in false positives, making it unmaintainable.

findings.section: Wave 5 — Bulk Swarm Approvals, Context Display, and Lifecycle Management
findings.message: The plan implements 'freezing' a rogue swarm but ignores the severe OS-level risks of suspending a process tree. If a suspended AI swarm process holds shared IPC locks, file handles, or UI threads (especially relevant for VS Code integrations), it will cause cascading deadlocks on the host OS. A maintainer will be unable to safely debug or resolve these freezes without a defined safe-suspend orchestration strategy or timeout fallback.

findings.section: Wave 6 — Historical Forensics UI and Resource Bounding
findings.message: The offline analysis bounds CPU (5%) and RAM (250MB), but completely ignores disk storage and I/O for system-wide ETW telemetry. ETW logs grow exponentially. Without a strict retention policy, log rotation, or circular buffer configuration defined in the plan, the feature will silently bloat the user's hard drive, leading to critical maintenance overhead and user complaints.
